Goal. Quantify how a single scalar clipping ratio α (applied at runtime to activation tensors in symmetric INT quantization) trades off quantization error vs. downstream language-modeling perplexity on LLAMA2-7B, given fixed asymmetric KV-cache quantization, and identify the α that best balances the two.

A. Locked setup (proposed).
  Model: LLAMA2-7B (FP16 reference).
  Weight quantization: per-channel symmetric INT, no clipping (fixed).
  Activation quantization: per-token symmetric INT, with hard clipping to ±α·max|x|.
  — If per-token (no α needed for activations) is preferred, say so.
  KV-cache quantization: asymmetric; K per-token (x_min,x_max), V per-channel (x_min,x_max).
  Precision: W4A4KV4 unless the flagged setup topics override.
  Calibration: a small (∼512 seq) wiki-style calibration set, separate from the ppl set.
  Evaluation: WikiText-2 raw test, sliding window 2048, ppl = exp(mean cross-entropy).

B. Sweep & design.
  α values (geometric, denser near 1):
   {1.000, 0.999, 0.995, 0.99, 0.985, 0.98, 0.97, 0.95, 0.93, 0.90, 0.85, 0.80, 0.70, 0.60, 0.50}
  Single-run per α; calibration tokens pre-quantized once and shared across α to keep storage bounded.
  Order α by reducing clipping magnitude (i.e. from 0.50→1.00) so that cumulative-error discussion in the writeup lines up.
  Optional arm: weight-clipping sweep at the same α values, to isolate where perplexity sensitivity comes from — only worth adding if U4 confirms clipping is applied to weights.

C. Endpoints & headline metrics.
  1. ppl(α) curve over the full sweep → plot onset of ppl rise vs. α.
  2. Δppl(α) = ppl(α) − ppl(FP16) → locate the smallest α where Δppl stays inside a quality budget (default budget: 0.3 nat; reportable as a sanity grid 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 1.0).
  3. argmin_α ppl(α) over the searched set → the empirical "optimal clipping ratio".
  4. Knee α via second-derivative test on the ppl-vs-α curve for robustness to evaluation noise.
  5. Calibration-quantization-error proxy: per-layer mean squared error after applying clipping at α, used only as a post-hoc check on the ppl curve.

D. Controls / feasibility checks (no execution now, but listed so the design is auditable).
  Sanity 1: α = 1.0 reproduces the "symmetric INT, no clipping" baseline; ppl should match published FP16→INT numbers within rounding.
  Sanity 2: full precision (FP16) ppl matches the published ~5.47 on WikiText-2 for LLAMA2-7B.
  Sanity 3: asymmetric KV-cache alone (no activation clipping) reproduces the paper's W4A4KV4 reference number within tolerance.
  TODO items in the writeup: exact calibration-file name, exact token count per sliding window, exact asymmetric KV granularity (per-token K / per-channel V), and how zero-point rounding is implemented (round-to-nearest-even).

E. Items requiring researcher confirmation before I lock the design.
  U1 – sweep range (default above)
  U2 – scope of α (activations only, or also weights)
  U3 – activation / KV granularity
  U4 – precision (W4A4KV4 default)
  U5 – evaluation set
  U6 – the "optimal" criterion (argmin ppl vs. Δppl-budget knee)
  U7 – single-run, no std
  U8 – values of neurips2024/94328/2:setup_1, setup_10, setup_17 (precision, granularity, sweep); please paste or summarize.
